summary: Reproduced two ROCDL objects for one gfx1201 kernel, removed the bare construction-time target so rocdl-attach-target is the sole target source, and added a regression proving the sole serialized object carries fast/unsafe compile hints.

tests.what_was_measured: One kernel produced two GPU objects; object 0 was bare and object 1 carried fast, unsafe_math, and no_wave64.
The preserved regression failed because the selected binary contained two ROCDL objects.
One kernel produced exactly one GPU object carrying fast, unsafe_math, and no_wave64.
The regression passed with exactly one hinted ROCDL object.
Executed on MI350X/gfx950 with zero error against a CPU PyTorch reference; one hinted GPU object was present and emitted gfx950 ISA contained loads, FP32 add, store, and end-program instructions.
30 focused tests passed and 2 pre-existing tests were skipped, covering compile hints, external codegen, backend registration, and real pointer vector-add execution.

gpu_execution_evidence: reports/j-7f247eb236d3/validate_gfx950.py ran on AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950:sramecc+:xnack- with max_abs_error=0 against a CPU-side PyTorch reference; raw output and ISA are under /job/job-artifacts/j-7f247eb236d3/.
remaining_limitations: The original gfx1201 case was validated compile-only because the assigned GPU is gfx950. Default-valued ROCDL options are canonicalized out of printed target attributes; fast, unsafe_math, and no_wave64 are directly visible on the sole gfx1201 object, while the pipeline source supplies O=2, abi=600, correct-sqrt=true, daz=false, and finite-only=false. No native C++ code changed.
